title: WHY SEA OTTERS NEVER STOP GROOMING
caption: Sea otters stay warm with a remarkable fur-care routine. 🦦 #SeaOtter #OceanLife #AnimalBehavior #WildVox

narration_timeline.text: Why does a sea otter spend so much time floating and fussing with its fur?
narration_timeline.scene: Open on real sea otter at water surface, preferably rubbing or grooming.

narration_timeline.text: Unlike seals, sea otters have very little blubber to help them stay warm.
narration_timeline.scene: Establish real sea otter in water, no unrelated seal footage.

narration_timeline.text: Instead, their incredibly dense coats trap insulating air right next to the skin.
narration_timeline.scene: Show genuine sea otter body and fur, with no invented microscopic closeup.

narration_timeline.text: But dirty or matted fur loses that protection, so grooming really matters.
narration_timeline.scene: Use real close sea otter movement while explaining the insulation mechanism.

narration_timeline.text: They rub, roll, and comb through their coats while resting on the surface.
narration_timeline.scene: Show documented sea otter rolling or grooming if present in selected clip.

narration_timeline.text: That constant care helps a sea otter survive in cold coastal water.
narration_timeline.scene: Finish on a wild sea otter afloat, resolving why the fur care matters.
